KOH.source: International Critical Tables vol. 3 (1928) p. 86, KOH, d4 at 15 °C (subset of 1 %-step table; also Perry's 8th ed. Table 2-78)
KOH.note: T = 15 °C (no reliable 20 °C table found). The CRC 20 °C KOH column (10 % 1.0873, 30 % 1.2813, 40 % 1.3881, 50 % 1.5024) is 0.3-0.8 % lower than ICT and than OxyChem Caustic Potash Handbook Table 1 (15.6 °C: 10 % 1.092, 30 % 1.292, 50 % 1.516 SG) and the Rauscher/Merck 20 °C table on Steffen's pages (1.090 <-> 9.96 %, 1.290 <-> 30.21 %, 1.510 <-> 49.95 %), far more than the 5 K temperature difference explains (~ -0.0003 to -0.0006 per K), so ICT 15 °C was used. Expect 20 °C values ~0.0015-0.003 lower.

H2O2.note: T = 18 °C: no full-range 20 °C table found. 20 °C cross-check: Evonik (manufacturer) 30 % 1.111, 35 % 1.131, 50 % 1.195, 70 % 1.289, 100 % 1.450; de.wikipedia (Ullmann) 35 % 1.1312, 50 % 1.1953, 70 % 1.2886, 90 % 1.3920 -> ICT 18 °C values are 0.001-0.002 higher, as expected for 2 K. Exception: 100 % (ICT 1.4465 at 18 °C vs modern 1.450 at 20 °C) - the old ICT value for nearly pure H2O2 is ~0.005 low; use the >90 % end with caution.

HClO4.note: The CRC table has no HClO4; ICT vol. 3 p. 54 (= Perry's Table 2-69) gives 20 °C only for 26-70 % and is 0.002-0.004 lower (30 % 1.2013 vs 1.204, 50 % 1.4018 vs 1.405, 70 % 1.6680 vs 1.672), while ICT 15 °C agrees with NBS 15 °C within 0.001 up to 60 % (10 % 1.0597 vs 1.060, 40 % 1.2991 vs 1.2985, 60 % 1.5389 vs 1.539). NBS 25 °C gives 1.664 for 70 %. 70 % at 20 °C = 1.672 (slightly above the expected 1.66-1.67).

HBr.note: de.wikipedia: 65 % HBr has density 1.7675 at room temperature (identical to ICT 20 °C). en.wikipedia 48 % ~1.49 vs ICT 45 % 1.4446 / 50 % 1.5173. Perry's Table 2-57 reproduces only the 4, 10 and 25 °C columns of this ICT table (its 25 °C column matches ICT, e.g. 1 % 1.0041, 65 % 1.7613).

HF.source: International Critical Tables vol. 3 (1928) p. 54, HF, d4 at 20 °C column (Perry's 8th ed. Table 2-60 reproduces the 10 %-step subset)
HF.note: Perry's 20 °C values (5 % 1.017, 10 % 1.035, 20 % 1.070, 30 % 1.101, 40 % 1.130, 50 % 1.155) identical. en.wikipedia: 48 % ~1.15 (ICT 45-50 %: 1.143-1.155, consistent). de.wikipedia quotes 1.14 for the 38 % azeotrope, ~0.015 above ICT (35 % 1.116 / 40 % 1.130). ICT gives 20 °C data only up to 50 % (higher concentrations only at 0 °C).

HCOOH.source: International Critical Tables vol. 3 (1928) pp. 122-123, "CH2O2, Formic acid", 20 °C column (reproduced in Perry's 8th ed. Table 2-108); subset of the 1 %-step table
HCOOH.note: CRC concentrative table only reaches 68 % (85th ed.) / 70 % (97th ed.) and is systematically lower than ICT (10 % 1.0224 vs 1.0246, 36 % 1.0839 vs 1.0871, 60 % 1.1364 vs 1.1424, 70 % 1.1586 vs 1.1655), so a CRC+ICT splice would be inconsistent; the single full-range ICT table was used instead. ICT 100 % (1.2212) agrees with the usual pure-acid value (de.wikipedia/GESTIS: 1.22 g/cm3 at 20 °C), and ICT 20 °C is consistent with its own 0/15/30 °C columns. Perry's reproduction has a misprint at 80 % (1.1806); the ICT scan reads 1.1860. The ICT 20 °C column is somewhat irregular in the last digit.

HCHO.source: J. F. Walker, "Formaldehyde" (ACS Monograph, Reinhold, 1944), Table 8 "Density and Refraction of Aqueous Formaldehyde" (data of Natta & Baccaredda), density at 18 °C; pure (methanol-free) aqueous formaldehyde, w = g CH2O / 100 g solution
HCHO.note: ASSUMES METHANOL-FREE solutions. Commercial formalin (37 %) usually contains methanol stabiliser, which lowers the density: Walker Table 4 (same authors, 18 °C, 37 % CH2O) gives 1.1128 (0 % MeOH), 1.1009 (5 %), 1.0890 (10 %), 1.0764 (15 %), 1.0639 (20 % MeOH). Cross-check with Walker Table 7 (Auerbach & Barschall, 18 °C): 18.82 % 1.0568, 37.53 % 1.1158 - consistent within ~0.001. The source lists the 0 % point (water at 18 °C). The 45->50 % step (1.1382->1.1570) is larger than the others, as printed.
